Meta today announced a series of new security features for WhatsApp, including expanded passkey support and a stronger two-step verification mechanism. Details below.

WhatsApp announces account security features

Meta today announced that WhatsApp now supports the use of more than one passkey for the same account, which is good news for users who use both iOS and Android devices.

WhatsApp says that more than 1 billion people now use a passkey to log back into their accounts using Face ID, Touch ID or a screen lock passcode. The company first launched passkey support on Android in October 2023, and extended it to iPhone in April the following year.

Additionally, WhatsApp today also announced that the two-step verification feature will be expanded from the original six-digit PIN code to support full alphanumeric passwords, including special characters.

WhatsApp explains: "Two-step verification is an extra layer of protection that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they obtain your one-time verification code." You can learn more here.

Finally, unfortunately this feature is currently only available on Android — WhatsApp will add a feature to make calls from unknown contacts safer and give users more confidence in answering them.

Press release content:

It is worth mentioning that iPhone users can also rely on a similar feature for handling traditional phone calls. Apple's Call Screening feature is available on iPhones running iOS 26, and will automatically ask unknown callers to state their name and reason for calling before the iPhone rings. Although this feature does not apply to WhatsApp calls, you can learn more about it here.
